newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 10.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Monday:
* On Friday, the Dow Jones rose 82.74 points to 6,855.80. PLDT's ADR gained $0 1/2 to $59 1/2.
* The peso closed weaker at 26.348 to a U.S. dollar from 26.341.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index inched up 10.71 points to 3,381.84.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was at 10.53125 percent from 10.5625.
* The Central Bank approves rules and regulations covering the flotation of Europeso bonds by financial institutions in the international capital markets. (MANILA BULLETIN)

* Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad says Malaysian investors will cut their investments in the Philippines on the recent decision by the Philippine Supreme Court to stop the sale of the Manila Hotel to Malaysia Renong Limited. (MALAYA, TIMES JOURNAL, INQUIRER, MANILA TIMES, CHRONICLE)
* Energy Minister Francisco Viray says he sees oil prices to drop in the coming months due to the softening of the cost of crude in the world market. (MALAYA)

* Sales of passenger cars for the month of January reach 5,951 units, down by 15.4 percent or 1,026 units from 7,037 units in January last year, the Chamber of Automotive Manufacturers of the Philippines Inc said. (JOURNAL, CHRONICLE)

* Smart Communications Inc, the telecommunications arm of Metro Pacific Corp, says to invest 15 billion pesos over the next two years to finance the expansion of its cellular phone operations and landline programme. (MANILA TIMES)
* Equitable Banking Corp says it will offer 25 percent of shares to the public by the middle of this month (CHRONICLE)
* The Central Bank says it is inclined to allow commercial banks to grant loan guarantees, paving the way for the effective increase in the single borrower's limit on banks.
